Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

define verb

also definition, give a definition

classical

Cic. Off. 1.7: ante dēfīnīre, quid sit officium
Traupman 246, 302

dēfīniō, dēfīnīre, dēfīnīvī, dēfīnītum

verb, fourth conjugation

define, say what a thing is

With an object or an indirect question (quid sit). Lewis & Short: first “to set bounds to”, then “to define”, frequent in Cicero.

Other words

  • fīniō, fīnīre, fīnīvī, fīnītum — define

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Quint. 12.1.1: quī ā M. Catōne fīnītur; Quint. 7.3.3 (Lewis & Short): ut sī fīniās equum

    Quintilian’s usual word for defining.

  • dēfīnītiō, dēfīnītiōnis f. — a definition

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.7: dēbet ā dēfīnītiōne proficīscī

    Lewis & Short: “freq. only in Cicero”.

Examples

  • Placet igitur, quoniam omnis disputātiō dē officiō futūra est, ante dēfīnīre, quid sit officium

    So, since this whole discussion is to be about duty, I think we should first define what duty isCic. Off. 1.7

  • sit ergō nōbīs ōrātor, quem cōnstituimus, is, quī ā M. Catōne fīnītur, vir bonus dīcendī perītus

    let the orator we are shaping, then, be the one Marcus Cato defined: a good man skilled in speakingQuint. 12.1.1

See also explain, mean, word.
